simple.meaning: שֵׁנָה (shênâh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “sleep.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 23 times in Genesis, Judges, Esther, Job, Psalms, and 5 more, beginning at Genesis 28:16. The surrounding contexts include family line, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שֵׁנָה (H8142) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: שֵׁנָה (shênâh) / H8142 is traced through Genesis 28:16, Genesis 31:40, Judges 16:14, Judges 16:20 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H8142. shenah or shena שְׁנָת שֵׁנָא, שֵׁנָה, noun feminine sleep — שֵׁנָה Psa 90:5 3 t.; שֵׁנָא 127:2 , שְׁנָת 132:4 (Ges § 80 g, h .); construct שְׁנַת Jer 51:39 3 t.; שְׁנָתִי Gen 31:40 ; Jer 31:26 , etc.; plural absolute שֵׁנוֺת Prov 6:10 ; 24:33 ; — sleep Gen 28:16 (J), Judg 16:14 , 20 ; Prov 3:24 ; 6:9 ; 20:13 ; Eccl 5:11 ; Jer 31:26 ; Zech 4:1 ; Prov 6:4 (|| תְּנוּמָה ); תְּנוּמוֺת מְעַט שֵׁנוֺת מְעַט 6:10 = 24:33 (these two of sluggard עָצֵל אִישׁ ; see also 6:9 ; 20:13 ); note also מֵעֵינָ֑י שְׁנָתִי וַתִּדּד Gen 31:40 (E) and my sleep fled from mine eyes ; הַמֶּלֶךְ שְׁנַת נָ֑דֲדָה Est 6:1 ; שְׁנָתָם וְנִגְזְלָה Prov 4:16 ; עָלָיו נִהְיְתָה וּשְׁנָתוֺ Dan 2:1 ; רֹאֵה אֵינֶנּוּ בְּעֵינָיו שֵׁנָה Eccl 8:16 ; לְעֵינָ֑י שְׁנָת אֶתֵּן אִם Psa 132:4 (all of lack of sleep); שֵׁנָ֑א לִידִידוֺ יִתֵּן 127:2 = he giveth to his beloved in sleep , compare Ges § 118 , 3; of sleep of death (so Arabic Dozy ii. 806 ) Job 14:12 ; Psa 90:5 (compare De Che); so, as accusative of congnate meaning with verb, 76:6 ; Jer 51:39 , 57 (in these two שְׁנַתעֿוֺלָם ). יֶשְׁנוֺ see יֵשׁ .

occurrences.englishText: Jacob awakened out of his sleep, and he said, “Surely Yahweh is in this place, and I didn’t know it.”
This was my situation: in the day the drought consumed me, and the frost by night; and my sleep fled from my eyes.
She fastened it with the pin, and said to him, “The Philistines are on you, Samson!” He awakened out of his sleep, and plucked away the pin of the beam and the fabric.
She said, “The Philistines are upon you, Samson!”
On that night, the king couldn’t sleep. He commanded the book of records of the chronicles to be brought, and they were read to the king.
so man lies down and doesn’t rise.
At your rebuke, God of Jacob,
You sweep them away as they sleep.
It is vain for you to rise up early,
When you lie down, you will not be afraid.
For they don’t sleep unless they do evil.
Give no sleep to your eyes,
How long will you sleep, sluggard?
A little sleep, a little slumber,
Don’t love sleep, lest you come to poverty.
a little sleep, a little slumber,
When goods increase, those who eat them are increased; and what advantage is there to its owner, except to feast on them with his eyes?
When I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done on the earth (even though eyes see no sleep day or night),
On this I awakened, and saw; and my sleep was sweet to me.
When they are heated, I will make their feast,
I will make her princes, her wise men,
In the second year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuchadnezzar dreamed dreams; and his spirit was troubled, and his sleep went from him.
The angel who talked with me came again, and wakened me, as a man who is wakened out of his sleep.
